title: Regional GPU utilization forecast — pool heatmaps and daily exports (Nov 2025)
content:
Executive summary:
This export is a compact capacity planning sheet derived from our daily/weekly GPU utilization dashboards across clusters and pools for the period 2025-10-20 -> 2025-11-02. It combines observed utilization (live metrics), short-term forecast (7d ARIMA-lite), and recommended scaling knobs for Dedicated and Private tenants. Main takeaways:
- Overall fleet avg utilization: 62% (last 14 days rolling average).
- Hot region: eu-central-1 pools showing sustained 78% avg; saturation windows during 09:00-12:00 CET weekdays.
- Burst pools (ap-southeast-1-burst) show high variance: 95th pct 90%, median 40% — indicates inefficient provisioning for short spikes.
- Preemptible capacity contribution: 12% of effective available GPUs; reduces peak risk but increases eviction churn.
- Forecast: if growth continues at observed 6% weekly traffic growth, eu-central-1 will exceed the soft-75% target in ~10 days, recommend adding 48 GPUs or shifting some inference routes to us-west-2 varints.

Data provenance and methodology:
- Source dashboards: Metrics pulled from /dashboards/infra/gpu-utilization (Prometheus via Grafana export).
- Time granularity: 1h rolling samples aggregated to daily/weekly metrics. This sheet includes daily max/avg/min per pool + 7-day forecast column.
- Forecast model: lightweight seasonal ARIMA with day-of-week covariate and rolling 14-day window weights. Not a product-grade predictor — used as signal for operational planning.
- Definitions: Pool = logical grouping (e.g., prod-infer-p1), Cluster = physical cluster (region+rack-level). Utilization = (vGPU active cycles / vGPU capacity) aggregated by GPU count; values shown as percent.

Daily export (sample slice: 2025-11-01):
CSV columns: date,region,cluster,pool,gpu_count,avg_util_pct,max_util_pct,min_util_pct,75th_pct,95th_pct,preemptible_pct,notes
2025-11-01,us-west-2,usw2-prod,prod-infer-p1,96,61,88,12,73,94,5,weekday morning spike at 11:00
2025-11-01,eu-central-1,euc1-prod,prod-infer-p2,64,78,100,45,85,100,8,steady high usage, consider scale up
2025-11-01,ap-southeast-1,apse1-burst,burst-pool-1,32,42,95,4,56,90,30,short short-lived spikes from batch jobs
2025-11-01,us-east-1,use1-ded,ml-dedicated-pool,128,55,70,22,62,80,0,stable

Weekly summary (rolling week ending 2025-11-02):
- us-west-2 (prod clusters): capacity 480 GPUs total across 5 pools; avg utilization 58%, 95th 91%. Observed 6% weekly growth.
- eu-central-1: capacity 192 GPUs; avg utilization 74%; weekday 09-13 CET average 86%.
- ap-southeast-1: capacity 96 GPUs (mix of burst/preemptible); high variance, 30% preemptible usage.

Anomaly flags (auto-detected):
- euc1-prod/prod-infer-p2: 3 consecutive days with >90% 95th percentile. Flag: "soft-capacity-exhaustion".
- apse1-burst/burst-pool-1: repeated >60% eviction rate on preemptible nodes during daily batch window. Flag: "eviction-churn-high".

Operational recommendations:
1) Short-term (0-2 weeks):
   - Add 48 Ni100-equivalent GPUs to eu-central-1 (prefer Dedicated pool) OR implement traffic split to us-west-2 for non-latency-sensitive routes. Estimated cost delta: +$12k/month.
   - Convert 25% of ap-southeast burst capacity to non-preemptible for 12 hours/day between 02:00-08:00 UTC to absorb batch spikes.
2) Mid-term (2-8 weeks):
   - Tune autoscaler policy for burst pools: lower cooldown to 2m, enable rapid scale out for >75% sustained 5m avg.
   - Experiment with prefix KV caching on eu-central-1 hot routes (expected token-cost reduction, could lower perceived load by 8-12%).
3) Long-term (quarterly):
   - Rebalance reserved commits: move 40 committed GPUs from east-coast reserved pool to eu committed capacity to match demand.
   - Evaluate on-prem placement for EU-heavy customers to reduce cross-region cost and latency.

Capacity planning appendices (short):
- Heatmap view recommended: rows = pool, columns = hour-of-day (UTC), cell = median util pct; generate weekly diffs to surface pattern shifts.
- Alert thresholds: create two alerts per pool: 95th>92% sustained for 6h (page), 75th>85% for 12h (ops-notify).

Open questions / action items:
- [@Priya] Confirm whether we can re-route non-SLA inference traffic for models m-commons-v3 and m-llama-7b to us-west-2 without regression tests. (linked: JIRA-9321)
- [@Miguel] Validate GPU type parity (Ni100 vs A100) cost/latency impact before we finalize eu-central-1 add.
- [@Liam] Prototype autoscaler change in staging cluster (use feature-flagged rollout).

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet intentionally keeps raw hourly dumps out of Drive; full raw exports are in gs://redwood-infra-exports/gpu-dumps/2025-11/ and summarized here.
- If accepted, I will convert these rows into a weekly shared Sheet with embedded heatmap for Product and SRE review.

Prepared by: Asha Kumar (infra capacity planning)
Reviewed: Priya Shen, Miguel Ortega, Liam O'Connor
Last figures refreshed: 2025-11-02 23:00 UTC
